sion reactor and intended for connection of a resistor for short-time service in order to increase the resistive component of the earth fault current. The loading duration of the secondary winding shall be specified. 3 RATING

1SCOPE 1.1Arc suppression
reactors covered by this standard (-Part 7 ) are single-phase reactors used to compensate for the capacitive current occurring in the case of line-to-earth faults in a system with an insulated neutral. They are connected between the neutral of a power transformer or an earthing transformer and earth in the case of a poly-phase system. Arc-suppression reactors may be specified with the inductance variable, either in steps or continuously over a specified range to permit tuning with the network capacitance. Arc-suppression reactors may be provided with a secondary winding for connection of a resistor and/or an auxiliary winding for measuring purposes. 2 TERMINOLOGY 2.0 For the purpose of this standard ing definitions shall apply. 2.1 Rated Voltage The rated voltage is the voltage at rated frequency assigned to be applied between the terminals of the main winding. This assigned voltage to be applied between the terminals of the main winding. This value is equal to the highest voltage which can occur between the neutral of the transformer or earthing couplers and earth during an earth fault. NOTE - Generally the rated voltage is approximately equivalent to the line-to-neutral voltage.

3.1The rated current shall be specified
less than the highest value of current recognized system earth fault conditions.

NOTE - If several successive faults may occur within a short period of time, the duration, the interval of time between applications and ttie number of applications shall be specified by th'e purchaser. The specified rated short-time current duration shall be selected accordingly.

4 ADJUSTMENT the follow-

RANGE

4.1 The current corresponding to rated voltage at rated frequency may be altered in one of the following ways: a) by adding additional sections of winding infinite steps with a off-load or on-load tap changer. b) by altering the air gap of the magnetic circuit with an adjustment mechanism.!
NOTE - In the case of adding additional sections of winding an adjustment range of not more than 2.5 is recommended.

5 WINDING

TEMPERATURE

RISE

2.2 Rated Current The current flowing through the main winding when rated voltage is applied at rated frequency, which the reactor is designed to carry for a specified duration. If the inductance is variable over a certain range either in steps of continuously the rated current refers-to minimum inductance. 2.3 Adjustment Range The ratio between the rated current and the lowest current obtainable by adjustment. 2.4 Auxiliary Winding A winding for measuring and control purpose, designed for a low voltage and a low current, . for instance 100 V, 10A.

5.1 The temperature rise of the windings of arcsuppression reactors at rated current shall not exceed the following values when tested according with 8.6.
NOTE -The values of temperature account the fact that system earth frequently and have limited duration. take into faults occur

The temperature rise limits are: - 80 K for continuous rated current. - 100K for maximum 2 hours specified duration of rated current. - 120 K for maximum 30 minutes ~specified duration of rated current. If short-time loading of a secondary winding for up to 10 minutes is specified its temperature shall not exceed the values prescribed for transformer widings under short-circuit conditions in IS 2026 ( Part 1 ) : 1977.

rs 5553'(Part `r ) : 199(9 6 INSULATION LEVEL 6.1 The insulation level shall correspond to the insulation level at the neutral of thi: system or to a lower insulation level specified on grounds of special measures used ( for example, surge arresters ). For the earth terminal of the main winding, the selection of a reduced insulation level should be appropriate ( non-uniform insulation ). For values of insulation levels see IS 2026 .(.Part 3 ) : 1981. Information on arc-suppression reactor insulation requirements and dielectric ,tests shall be supplied by the prospective purchaser. 7 RATING PLATES 7.5 Each arc-suppression -reactor shall be provided with a rating plate of weather-proof material, fitted in a visible position, showing the appropriate items as follows. 8.4 Measurement of Current The measurement shall be made over the whole range of adjustment, preferably at rated frequency. If this is impracticable the test voltage should be chosen as high as possible and test at different voltages should be made for the purpose of extrapolation. 2

IS 5553 ( Part 7 )

: 1990

8.5 Measurement of No-Load Voltage The measurement of the no-load voltages of the auxiliary and secondary winding shall be made over the whole range of adjustment, at rated voltage on the main winding. 8.6 Temperature Rise Test The measurement shall be made with open terminals of auxiliary and secondary winding in accordance with 4 of IS 2026 ( Part 3 ) : 1981. The initial value of the top oil temperature shall be equal to the cooling air temperature. The winding temperature shall in principle be ascertained using the resistance method immediately after the end of the rated loading duration. 8.7 Dielechic Tests The rated withstand voltages are verified by the following dielectric tests: a) Uniform hwlation: i) Separate source power-frequency withstand test (see 10 of ( Part 3 > : 1981 ); voltage IS 2026

If the induced overvoltage withstand test is impracticable the test shall be replaced by a lightning `impulse test subject to agreement between In this the purchaser and the manufacturer. case, however, a longer duration of the impulse voltage front time is allowed - up to 13 ps. In the case of windings with additional sections the lightning impulse test shall be made on both maximum and minimum positions. 9 TOLERANCES 9.1 Table 1 gives tolerances to be applied to certain rated quantities and to other quantities when they are the `subject of the manufactu.-er's guarantees referring to this standard. Standard Mark
I

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of the Indian Standards, Act, 2986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 1 that standard as a further safeguard. of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from ' the Bureau (.fIndian Standards.
